Cleanse thou thyself, then cleanse thou the people with this Kawthar that hath descended from the right hand of the Throne, wherewith are sanctified the hearts of the knowing. Admonish thine own soul, then admonish the people, that thy word may be preferred in all the worlds. Thus hath the Tongue of power and majesty taught thee. And who is more truthful than God in speech, if ye be of them that are assured?

And if thou journey to another land and any should inquire of the Youth of the Spirit, say: "I left Him at the hour when His garment was sprinkled with the blood of hatred, and the darknesses of the earth encompassed Him from every side, whilst He cried out among them with a cry whereat all things were shaken—whatsoever hath been created betwixt earth and heaven." Thus was the matter, if ye be of them that know. And He saith: "O people! Slay not the Youth after He hath come unto you from the direction of holiness with a clear Book. O people! I speak not of mine own desire, but according to what the Mighty in Power teacheth Me from the dominion of God, the Most High, the All-Glorious. Beware lest ye smite Me with the swords of self and passion. Fear God, unto Whom all things return, if ye be of them that believe."

> "O people! This is ʿAli amongst you, reciting unto you that which was recited aforetime; all atoms bear witness thereto. This is the resplendent, mighty, and impregnable Tablet. O people! If ye disbelieve in these Messengers, by what proof then believed ye in the Messengers of God before? Bring forth your evidence, if ye be of them that speak the truth. Marvel ye that the Youth of God hath come unto you in the form of a mortal like unto yourselves, casting upon you the verses of your Lord, and teaching you the paths of knowledge and of gnosis, that He may draw you nigh unto the radiant, sanctified, and luminous Beauty of God? Thus do thou remind the servants, that perchance there may be kindled within their hearts the fire of God and His love, and that they may arise to remember Him and to praise Him, and may become of the helpers."

Say: O people! Come ye unto a just word between us and you: If ye aid not your Lord, the All-Merciful, ye cannot harm Him; and if ye uphold Him not, ye cannot betray Him. Be ye equitable in the Cause of your Lord, and be not of them that turn away. Say: He, verily, knoweth the unseen of the heavens and of the earth; and He knoweth what your hands perform, what your hearts conceal, and what your tongues utter. This is the truth, the certitude. He rewardeth every soul for that which it hath earned; and the recompense of the unjust is naught but the lowest depths of the blazing Fire.

Say: O concourse of Bayan! If ye be in doubt concerning My religion, know ye that I have believed in God Who created you and all things. I will not follow you in your idle fancies. I have been commanded to worship none but Him; and I am the first of them that worship. Say: O people! Have mercy upon your own selves and upon the souls of men, and turn them not aside from the path of God that hath encompassed all things, if in His Cause ye would be of them that ponder. Read ye that which hath been revealed by the Pen of holiness; if ye find therein the fragrance of your Lord, deny it not, and be not of them that join partners with Him.

By God! This is His very Self, and these are His verses that have filled the East and the West of the earth. By what proof then do ye seek to argue, O people of the Furqan? Be ye fair, O company of the slanderers! God beareth witness that ye had before you naught save that which We revealed aforetime upon Our former Beauty; and this is what hath been sent down from His presence upon this radiant, resplendent, pearl-like Beauty. Ye shall, ere long, be questioned concerning that which ye have denied and from which ye have turned away; ye shall be requited for what ye have done, and shall become of them that work.

Say: He hath sent forth before Him and behind Him, and on His right hand, messengers, watchers, and bearers of glad tidings, proclaiming to every atom the lights that have shone forth from the Face of God, the All-Powerful, the Mighty, the Merciful. Say: Blind hath become the eye that loveth not to behold the Beauty of its Lord after He hath appeared in truth between the heavens and the earth. Thus have We cast upon the contingent beings every discourse, that perchance there may be enkindled within their hearts the fire of God, and that they may cry out:

> "There is none other God but Me, the Exalted, the Wise, the All-Knowing."

O Muhammad! When the fragrances of holiness have drawn thee and turned thee toward the realms of the All-Merciful, that thou mayest find the breaths of the All-Glorious, then go thou, by permission of thy Lord, the All-Bountiful, unto the station round which circle the angels of them that are nigh—who, around the Throne, do glorify God. And when thou dost arise from thy place and desire to turn unto the direction of God, thy Lord, cast off from thy body the garment of self and passion, and from thy feet the two sandals of oppression and lewdness; for thou art entering a station into which none shall come save he who leaveth behind him all that is on earth and in heaven, and none shall be accepted save the sanctifying of the Most Greatness, if thou be of them that comprehend. Round about it circle Sinai of glory, and the Mount of command, and the wilderness of holiness, and the hearts of them who, at every moment, ascend unto the air of nearness. Without this thou shalt not attain, nor shalt thou be remembered with God among them that enter therein, though thou abide therein a thousand years of the years ye reckon.

And when thou hast migrated from thyself and from the world and its people, and hast journeyed unto God, thy Lord, and hast reached the station where thou beholdest the blackness of the City, then alight, stand upon thy place, and say:

> "Spirit, light, glory, and praise be upon thee, O City of God and dwelling-place of His Names, treasury of His Attributes, source of His outpourings, mine of His bounties, and the Manifestation of His revelations that have encompassed all existence. I bear witness that from thy dark soil there hath appeared the Point of Firstness, the broidering of pre-existence, the ancient mystery, the all-embracing Word, the irrevocable decrees, and the treasured secrets. Thus hath grace preceded from God, the All-Sovereign, the Self-Subsisting."

Then raise thou thy hands unto God, thy Lord, in lowliness and awe and submission and a beloved contentment, and say:

> "O my Lord! Praise be unto Thee for the wonders of Thy gifts and the subtleties of Thy bestowals. How shall I thank Thee, O my God, for having granted me the visitation of Thy House, and for having honoured me thereby, and for having singled me out with this favour wherewith none before me hath been favoured, and for having taught me that which no soul besides me hath known? Wherefore, O my God, I have fled from the house of mine own self and have clung to the most exalted seat of Thy Self; I have escaped from that which withheld me from Thy nearness and have sought refuge in the precincts of Thy most great mercy. Therefore, O my God, deprive me not of that which is with Thee, and occupy me not with aught beside Thee. Verily Thou art the Mighty, the All-Forgiving. O my Lord! Confirm me in Thy love and the love of Thy chosen ones, and make me not of those who deny Thy verses after their revelation and mock them after their breaths have encompassed the contingent beings and all that hath been created in the realms of the unseen and the seen. O my Lord! Bestow upon me, from Thy presence, the staff of Thy grace and Thy care, that I may cleave asunder therewith the sea of self and passion, and pass beyond it to reach the tents of the glory of Thy tenderness and the pavilion of the holiness of Thy infallibility, lest there appear from me that which Thy good-pleasure abhorreth. Thou, verily, doest whatsoever Thou willest, and Thou art the Lord of this inhabited House."

### Section 3: “Then mount and ride on until thou reachest…” {.unnumbered}

Then mount and ride on until thou reachest a station where naught remaineth betwixt thee and the City save a thousand paces—more or less. Then alight, and immerse thyself in water, even as thou hast been bidden in the Book of God, the All-Sovereign, the Exalted, the Self-Subsisting. And when thou comest forth from the water, trim thou thy moustache, then pare thy nails, and shave thy head; then make use of the choicest perfumes, and clothe thyself, as far as thou art able, in the fairest raiment. And if thou be not able to do that which We have commanded thee, grieve thou not; God hath, verily, pardoned thee, and He is the All-Powerful, the Forgiving, the Tender-Merciful.

Then strive within thine own soul that, when thine eye falleth upon the City and thou drawest nigh unto it, thy heart may be cleansed of the remembrance of created things, in such wise that thou leavest behind thee all that hath been created between the earths and the heavens; for then shalt thou be walking in the presence of the Sovereign of contingent beings and the King of Names and Attributes. Thus doth the Pen of God, thy Lord and the Lord of all things, instruct thee, if ye but know.

And when thou hast fulfilled that which We have enjoined upon thee, arise from thy place, then turn thy face toward the House; stand, and lift up thine hands in supplication unto God, the All-Powerful, the All-Sovereign, the Beloved, and say:

> "O my God! This is the station whereby the eyes of the longing are comforted, and the hearts of the lovers are drawn. This is the ultimate goal of them that seek, and the highest desire of the yearning. This is the station wherein the eyes of the knowing rain tears in their separation from Thee, and the faces of them that have attained grow pale through their longing for Thy beauty. I beseech Thee, O my God, by it, and by the effulgent splendours of the lights of the glory of Thine oneness, and by the flashing brilliance of the manifestations of the holiness of Thy divinity, to deliver me from the fire of mine own self, and to sanctify me from all that beseemeth not Thy sovereignty. Verily Thou art the All-Sovereign, the Self-Subsisting."

Then lower thine hands until they reach thy thighs; then magnify God nine times. Thereupon raise thou thine hands once more unto God, thy Lord and the Lord of what hath been and what shall be, and say:

> "My God! This is the City wherein Thy sovereignty hath appeared, the traces of the majesty of Thy glory have been made manifest, Thy verses have descended, Thy Word hath been fulfilled, Thy power hath been exalted, Thy proof hath shone forth, and Thy mercy hath encompassed all things and all that are in the heavens and on the earth. To this my soul and my heart and my tongue bear witness, and likewise the honoured servants. I beseech Thee, O my God, by it and by what hath been manifested therein, to remove from me whatsoever keepeth me far from the shore of the holiness of Thy mercy and bounty, and debarreth me from the precincts of the outpourings of Thy grace and bestowal. Then clothe me, O my God, with the robe of Thy munificence and Thy loving-kindness, for Thou art powerful to do what Thou willest, and Thou art the Mighty, the Exalted, the Beloved. Moreover, O my God, give me to drink of the Salsabil of the glory of the knowledge of Thee, and of the spring of the holiness of meeting Thee—so potent that, should but a drop thereof be sprinkled upon contingent beings, they would assuredly become living, abiding, everlasting, steadfast, facing Thy countenance and the manifestations of the flashing splendours of the lights of Thy dawning. Verily Thou art the Mighty, the Exalted, the All-Holy."

Then lower thine hands, and walk upon the earth with the dignity of God and His tranquillity; and in thy walking glorify thy Lord, then magnify Him, and sanctify Him, and exalt Him. Follow the ways of the Messengers and the character of them that are nigh, and say:

> "At Thy service, O God, at Thy service; at Thy service and at Thy good pleasure; and light is before Thee."

Repeat thou these words according to the measure of the fire of thy yearning and desire that shall not be quenched. Thus have We commanded thee in truth, that thou mayest be of them who act according to what they have been enjoined.

Know, moreover, that by this word thou art answering thy Lord at the hour when He established Himself upon the Throne, and called the contingent beings with His utterance, "Am I not your Lord?" This, verily, is the secret of this matter, could ye but ponder the mysteries of your Lord. Nay, if thou beholdest with the eye of innate perception, thou shalt then witness Him established upon the thrones of all created things, crying aloud: "There is none other God but Me, the All-Sovereign, the Self-Subsisting."

And thou, O visitor, recognize thy rank and thy measure at that hour; then give thanks unto God for that wherewith thou hast been endowed and strengthened. There is no God but Him. His is creation and command, and all do work by His behest. Happy art thou, O servant, in that thou hast entered the wilderness of holiness, and the Paran of the Spirit, and the Sinai of command. Nay, shouldst thou but sharpen thine sight, thou wouldst behold that all around thee circle. By God, O migrating servant! Were God to open thine eyes, and wert thou to lift up thy gaze above thy head unto the heaven, thou wouldst behold the sanctuaries of holiness, the retreats of intimacy, the dwellers within the pavilion of the divine Ipseity, the occupants of the seats of omnipotence, and the temples of the sanctified—manifestations of the realms of dominion and of the kingdom—all moving in the air of holiness above thee, and glorifying and magnifying and sanctifying and exalting with thee the Lord of the City, and Him Who hath appeared from it and arisen within it. Thus shalt thou witness the Cause, if thou be of them that see with the sight of the spirit.

And when thou hast reached a station such that thou art within twenty paces of the gate of the City, then stand, by the command of God, thy Lord and the Lord of all things, and the Lord of this praised scene. Then magnify God nineteen times; then address the City on My behalf and say:

> "May God curse a people who have come between us and the lights of Thy holy sanctity, O City of God; who have hindered us from breathing in the fragrances of the holiness of Thine oneness, and from abiding in the precincts of the glory of Thy mercy, and from standing at the threshold of the gate of the outpouring of Thy merciful grace."

Then turn thou thine gaze unto the Most Great Scene, toward the wall of the City and whatsoever hath been created therein and was upon it; for upon all these hath fallen the glance of God, the Mighty, the All-Sovereign, the Self-Subsisting. Say:

> "O wall of the City! Blessed art thou, in that upon thee have shone forth the lights of the Sun of thy Lord, the Most High, the All-Exalted. O trees of the City! Blessed are ye, in that the breezes of holiness have blown upon you from the direction of everlastingness. O air of the City! Blessed art thou, in that within thee hath been spread the Breath of God, the Mighty, the All-Powerful, the Beloved. O earth of the City! Blessed art thou, in that upon thee hath trodden the Foot of thy Lord, the All-Merciful, and through thee hath passed the Temple of the All-Glorious, in the days when all were veiled within the coverings of their own selves."

Then walk on until thou reachest the City. And when thou hast attained unto meeting it, and hast come to its gate, lay thy face upon the dust of the gate, that thou mayest inhale the fragrance of thy Lord, the Most High, the All-Exalted, and mayest be of them who are nourished by the Water of Life. Know then that from its dust appeareth the ordinance of water, and from its water the ordinance of air, and from its air the trace of fire; and from a spark thereof hath appeared the decree of the Kaf and the Nun, if ye but know. Such is what We have described unto thee upon the earth and in the midst of those who, in the drunkenness of their own selves, are sunk in heedlessness. Otherwise—by Him in Whose hand is My soul!—a single atom of its dust is, in the sight of God, dearer than whatsoever hath been created in the meadows of eternity, and than whatsoever hath been decreed in the Tablets of destiny, in the mystery of consummation, in the dominion of primal beginning. Thus do We cast upon thee of the secrets of the Cause, that thou mayest be of them that understand.

And when thou hast kissed the dust and sought blessing thereby, lift up thy head, then arise and magnify God nineteen times; then glorify thy Lord with Baha nineteen times. Then walk with the dignity and tranquillity of God, and with His majesty and His grandeur, until thou standest facing the House; then halt and say:

> "I testify with my tongue, my soul, my spirit, and my body, that this is the station whereat bow down the denizens of the dominion of the Unseen, and thereafter the dwellers in the kingdom of primal decree, and then they that abide upon the broidered canopies of everlastingness beyond the billowing seas of grandeur. Through it hath everything been made manifest; through it pass the breezes of bounty over the temples of all the worlds. This is the station wherewith are blessed the inhabitants of the Concourse of Eternity, and by whose light are illumined the hearts of them that have been established between earth and heaven; its threshold is swept each day by the people of the crimson chambers, and thereafter by the locks of the Spirit the angels of them that are nigh. This is the station wherein the Beauty of the All-Merciful was revealed, then, by His own Self, He established Himself upon the Throne of forgiveness, and decreed what He willed concerning the peoples of the worlds. He, verily, doeth whatsoever He pleaseth; He ordaineth what He loveth, and accomplisheth what He desireth. I testify that from a handful of this dust was Adam, the First, created; therefore was he named the father of mankind in the kingdom of Names, and God appointed him the first of His remembrance among all created things."

Then cast thy face upon the dust, place thy right cheek thereon, and say:

> "Glory be to Thee, O God, my God! This is Thy servant who hath severed himself from every direction and turned toward the direction of Thy singleness; who hath delivered his soul from all save Thee and hath clung to the cords of the bounty of Thy care; who hath come, with his whole being, unto the plains of the glory of Thy mercifulness. Wherefore, O my God, breathe upon my heart of the winds of the glory of the holiness of Thy solicitude, and upon my very being of the fragrances of the sovereignty of the glory of Thy loving-kindness. Cast me not away, O my God, from Thy door, deprived; nor from the dawning-places of the Sun of Thy bounty, hopeless. Verily Thou art powerful to do what Thou willest, and Thou art the All-Sovereign, the Mighty, the Omnipotent."

Then arise and turn toward the right side of the House, unto the direction of thy Lord, the Exalted, the Mighty, the Wise. Lift up thy hands unto God, the Most High, the All-Exalted, and say:

> "Glory be to Thee, O God, my God! The hands of my hope have been raised unto the heaven of Thy bounty and Thy gifts, and the fingers of my reliance have been fastened to the cords of Thy grace and Thy loving-kindness. I beseech Thee by Him through Whom Thou hast arrayed contingent beings with the robes of Thy guidance, and quickened all created things through the sovereignty of Thy compassion and Thy generosity, that Thou shut not the door of Thy knowledge against the face of my heart, nor the gate of Thy mercy against my soul. Then make me, O my God, such as beseemeth the sovereignty of the glory of Thine oneness and the kingship of the holiness of Thy self-sufficiency; verily Thou art the Bountiful, the Bestowing, the Mighty, the Generous. And I, O my God, have severed myself from mine own self, hastened unto Thy Most Exalted Self, migrated from my house, and stood before Thy Most Pure, Most Glorious House. I beseech Thee that Thou leave me not to myself, nor to them that keep men from the love of Thy Beauty and turn the servants aside from Thy mighty and straight path."

### Section 4: “Then circumambulate the House on My behalf seven…” {.unnumbered}

Then circumambulate the House on My behalf seven times. Thus doth the Beauty of ancient days command thee, and teach thee what none in all the worlds can know. And while thou dost circle the House of thy Lord, remember Him in thine heart and upon thy tongue, and within thyself face the direction of a mighty Throne. When thou hast completed thy circumambulation, present thyself in the first portico opposite the gate of the Sanctuary; then stand, and raise thy hands unto the heaven of the outpouring of the grace of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Inaccessible.

And I enjoin thee that, when thou raisest thy hands, raise them with that attraction whereby the hands of all created things are lifted unto the heaven of thy Master's bounty; and when thou desirest to call upon God, thy Lord, call thou upon Him with that purity whereby the tongues of every atom utter praise of thy Creator and remembrance of thy Originator, the All-Powerful, the All-Strong, the Wondrous. For if thou be not thus, it beseemeth thee not to stand in the station wherein have stood the temples of the sanctified and the near ones, nor to be related unto Me, nor to abide beneath the shadow of My love—which God hath made a sharp sword between the idolaters and them that affirm His oneness.

And when thou raisest thy hands unto the clouds of the mercy of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Knowing, the All-Knowing, say:

"I testify that there is none other God but Him, alone, without partner, without peer, without minister, without equal, without adversary, without rival, without counterpart to His uplifted, inaccessible, exalted sovereignty. He hath ever been—one in His Essence, one in His attributes, one in His acts; and He shall ever remain even as He hath ever been, in the glory of His majesty and the dominion of His awe-inspiring power—He before Whose holiness the knowing confess their impotence to enter the realms of the sanctity of His knowledge, and the sincere acknowledge their failure to ascend unto the heaven of His remembrance and His praise. Verily He is the All-Sovereign over all things; verily He is the Mighty, the Gracious.

"And I testify that the Primal Point, our Lord, the Most High, is His manifestation in the heaven of the Unseen, His appearance in the dominion of decree, His dawning in the kingdom of irrevocable enactment. Through Him were all created things raised up, and all contingent beings renewed; through Him was the Balance of justice set upon a station of praised glory; through Him the cock of the Throne crowed and the dove of glory sang; through Him the Resurrection of the Cause was established and what had been treasured in the repositories of guarded might was disclosed. Through Him were the heavens of pre-existence uplifted, and the clouds of bounty ascended in this most holy, most noble expanse; through Him the Sun of grace and munificence shone forth from a radiant horizon of sanctity; through Him the seas of verses surged in the kingdom of names and attributes; and the appointed season of the Cause was fulfilled according to what had been ordained in the scrolls of inviolable glory.

"And I testify that through Him the veil of concealment was lifted from the Beauty of Grandeur, the mysteries of the unseen were made manifest in the kingdom of primal beginning; through Him every poor one hath mounted to the heaven of riches, every mortal hath ascended to the stations of abidingness, and every ailing one to the retreats of healing, beneath a pavilion of flashing light.

"And I testify, O my God, that this is the station wherein Thou didst establish Thyself upon the Throne of the glory of Thine oneness, and didst create the first and the last by the sovereignty of Thy will and Thy purpose; herein did the clouds of Thy favour rain upon all the worlds. Therefore I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy Most Great Name, the treasured and concealed, and by Thy most perfect Word, stored up in the hidden repositories—whereof Thou didst promise the servants the manifestation at the time of the Cry for Help—that Thou wouldst cause me to enter upon the shore of the ocean of Thy forgiveness, and wouldst blot out from me all that Thou hast numbered of my gravest offences and my mightiest sins.

"Then forgive, O my God, my father and my mother, my kindred, and those whom I have counted as belonging unto mine own self from among them that have believed in Thee and in Thy signs. Appoint for me, O my God, a seat of truth in Thy presence; then join me unto Thy near ones.

"And I beseech Thee, O my God and my Beloved, that Thou make me not of those who circumambulate Thy House upon Thy earth, yet deny Thy Sacred House in the Manifestations of Thy Self, the Dawning-Places of the glory of Thy Self-Subsisting might, the seats of the holiness of Thy Lordship. This, O my God, is the uttermost of my hope and my longing, and Thou art the Sovereign, the All-Powerful, the Mighty, the Wise.

Moreover I beseech Thee, O my God, by Thy Beauty whereby the suns of the glory of Thy care have been illumined, and the flashes of the lights of the holiness of Thy bounty have shone resplendent, that Thou stir me not with fear on the Day whereon every soul is shaken, every possessor of might and authority waxeth proud, the feet of them that have attained do slip, the clamour of all things is raised, and every shining light is darkened. Take Thou my hand, O my God, with the hand of Thy grace and Thy bounty. Deprive me not on that Day of the fragrances of the glory of Thy sanctity, nor of hearing the melodies of Thy wondrous utterance.

Set me not, O my God, behind every sinful crier. Make my sight, through Thy favour, opened wide, that I may know Thee by Thine own Self and not by aught beside Thee, and may behold the wonders of the lights of Thy Beauty through what Thou hast bestowed upon me of Thy bounty, and not through what is with men. For Thou hast not appointed for Thy Self any proof beside Thine Essence, nor any demonstration other than Thy signs. Verily Thou art the One Who standeth, the Judge, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. Praise be to God, the Lord of all things and the Lord of the worlds."

Then conclude thy visitation; for We have not permitted any to draw nigh unto the Sanctuary beyond this measure, inasmuch as before that station the lights of the Essence shine forth from behind names and attributes. Short of that is observed, for the sake of courtesy—courtesy which hath ever been among the fairest of qualities in the sight of God, the Possessor of the earths and the heavens. Thus have We delivered unto thee this ordinance with a proof that is clear, resplendent, and manifest.

Verily We love that from every city one should go forth on My behalf and of his own soul, that he may visit the House of God and be of them that visit. By God! at every step he taketh there descend mercy and loving-kindness from a radiant heaven of holiness; and when he lifteth the one foot and setteth it down, God forgiveth his sins and the sins of his mother and his father and all that is ascribed unto him. Thus hath the grace of thy Lord encompassed all created things, the first and the last. By God! He who visiteth the House is as he who hath visited God within the pavilion of the glory of His meeting and the tent of the majesty of His Beauty. Thus do We announce unto you tidings of that which, in the presence of the Throne, was accounted great.

And he who visiteth the House according to what We have taught him, God shall raise him after his death in the Ridvan of glory and grandeur, in such a form that the Concourse on high is illumined by the lights of his countenance; and He shall command all that are in the highest heavens to gather before him, to circle round him, and to visit his beauty at every morn and eventide.

O trustees of God upon the earth! Hasten unto the Most Great Remembrance; then leave what is in your hands, and turn your faces toward the Seat of God, the Mighty, the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing. Be steadfast, O people, in the station that, though all upon the earth rise up against you, ye shall not turn aside therefrom, but shall in the religion of God be of the firmly grounded. The idolaters will seek to withhold you from what God hath cast upon you, by reason of the rancour that is in their breasts; yet God doeth what He willeth by His word, and He is the All-Powerful, the Omnipotent.

Then know ye that We have written Tablets, detailed and expansive, concerning the visitation of the House, yet We have not sent them forth until this present hour. Were God to will, We would send them down in truth; verily, He is the Protector of the Messengers. That which We have sent down is this which hath been revealed, in brief, from the Kingdom of God; for the angels nigh unto Him and the denizens of the Concourse on high love, outwardly, to be concise in their observances, while inwardly they are, at every moment, numbered among them that visit. Thus have We taught you, made known unto you the paths of holiness, and guided you unto the shore of manifest grace.

And thou, O Muḥammad, when thou dost behold Karím in the city, call him to remembrance with a remembrance from Our presence; then gladden him with the tidings of a paradise of gracious holiness. Say: O Karím! Arise from thy place, then proclaim aloud betwixt the heavens and the earth that the mystery of the Cause hath been made manifest from the Dayspring of His wondrous Name. Rend asunder the veils of idle fancy, that from behind them the Beauty of the Ancient of Days may shine forth with the lights of a radiant glory.

Know thou, moreover, that the wine of divine intoxication hath encompassed all who dwell in the heavens and on the earth. Wherefore, come thou forth from behind the veils, that this upraised and luminous cloud may rain down upon thy heart. Then announce unto the people the Most Great Treasure, and remind them of this mighty Announcement.

Say: For twenty years We concealed Our countenance beneath seventy thousand veils, that none among the dwellers of the heavens and the earth might know Us. But when the idolaters—those in whose breasts lay rancour against the Youth—rose up in opposition unto Us, We unveiled the countenance of the Cause with manifest sovereignty. Thereupon the suns of vain imaginings were darkened, the moon of gloom was eclipsed, the stars of hatred fell upon the face of the earth, and the souls of the spiteful returned unto the lowest fire, the abode of the idolaters.

And thou, O Karím, tarry not for a single instant. Deliver then the Cause of thy Lord unto every knowing and discerning soul. By God! Whenever thou hearest that there hath appeared aught of My mighty and beauteous sovereignty, come forth from the chambers of sorrow, and loose thy tongue in utterance and exposition in remembrance of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Ruler, the Wise.

Then cast all who are upon the earth behind thee, lest aught thereof should hinder thee; that thou mayest become possessed of a rarefied, subtle, and unassailable lightness, and be enabled to soar into the atmosphere of nearness in this heaven which We have upraised through Our Name, the Most Exalted, the All-Powerful, the All-Knowing. Thus have We commanded thee and singled thee out from among the servants, that thou mayest arise for the Cause with sovereign power.
